region: Price optimisation (per-record gradient + ratebook coordinate descent; efficient frontier)
purpose: Constrained portfolio price-optimisation engine exposed as FastAPI endpoints. Given an optimiser node in a pipeline graph, it executes the upstream graph lazily to materialise a long-format scored DataFrame (one row per quote x scenario step), validates/projects it, builds a Rust QuoteGrid, and runs one of two solvers from the bundled `price_contour` library: (1) ONLINE mode = per-record Lagrangian dual decomposition (each quote independently picks the scenario step maximising obj + signed-lambda*constraint); (2) RATEBOOK mode = coordinate descent over rating-factor tables. It also computes the efficient frontier (sweep over constraint-threshold ranges), estimates achievable frontier ranges from the scenario envelope (auto-range), and supports apply/save/MLflow-log of solved lambdas/factor tables. Haute owns ALL orchestration, streaming/chunking, validation, artifact lifecycle, concurrency and result materialisation; the numerical kernels live in price_contour (Rust + thin Python).

public_surface: POST /api/optimiser/solve -> start background solve (online|ratebook), returns job_id
POST /api/optimiser/estimate -> quote/scenario counts via single streaming aggregation (solver not invoked)
POST /api/optimiser/frontier -> recompute efficient frontier for a completed job
POST /api/optimiser/frontier/select -> select a frontier summary point (materialises ratebook factor tables on demand)
POST /api/optimiser/apply -> per-quote detail preview (online only; ratebook rejected 422)
POST /api/optimiser/save -> write optimiser_result.json artifact (lambdas/factor tables) to a sandbox-validated path
POST /api/optimiser/mlflow/log -> log params/metrics/artifacts incl. complete apply artifact + frontier CSV
load_optimiser_artifact / load_mlflow_optimiser_artifact (consumed by OPTIMISER_APPLY node executor)
invariants: Solver input contract: scored frame is long-format with one row per (quote_id, scenario_index); quote_id must be Utf8/Categorical/Enum and non-null on EVERY row; objective/scenario_value/constraint columns must be finite at Float32 precision (NaN/inf rejected as a 400 contract error, never silently solved on — see _validate_input_value_contracts).
Column-dtype contract for the grid: scenario_index->Int32, scenario_value/objective/constraints->Float32; ratio-linearised synthetic column cast to Float32 (else QuoteGridBuilder rejects).

Ratebook factor-context alignment: factor contexts must carry a non-None quote_id_fingerprint that equals the QuoteGrid's 64-bit fingerprint and matching n_quotes; mismatch raises (price_contour _resolve_factor_contexts). Haute builds contexts with expected_quote_ids=grid.quote_ids so alignment holds by construction.

Ratebook factor-level canonicalisation (3b.10): saved factor-table level keys MUST equal what the apply-side rating join derives via normalise_rating_key (Float64 25.0 -> '25'); two emitted levels that collapse to one canonical key FAIL LOUDLY rather than last-writer-wins (would silently drop a solved rate).

Server-owned parquet artifacts (apply result, ratebook factors) must live under the resolved temp artifact root, use absolute paths, correct kind/version/format, the expected directory prefix and filename; path resolution must not escape the artifact root (_validate_server_owned_parquet_handle).
Save-path sandboxing: absolute output paths resolve against project root, relative against pipeline dir, then validate_safe_path enforces the boundary.

Frontier compute budget == library cap: the route gate (FRONTIER_COMPUTE_LIMIT=10000, strictly >) MUST equal price_contour max_total_points default so an admitted request never dies as an opaque 500 inside the library; pinned by test_optimiser_routes_real_library.

AUTO_RANGE projection subset invariant: auto_range_required_columns ⊆ solver_required_columns per node, so the opportunistic dataframe-execution cache warmed during auto-range can be reused (or correctly rejected) by a later solve without violating AUTO_RANGE's narrow-projection contract (_execute_pipeline comment, lines ~4199-4240).

Concurrency: only ONE blocking solve job may run at a time (estimate + auto-range are non-blocking); a graph/node single-flight key prevents concurrent setup for the same (graph_fingerprint,node); job-store updates are whole-dict atomic swaps so status pollers never see half-updated state.

Heavy-object lifecycle: solver/solve_result/quote_grid (+ratebook factor contexts/factors_df) are retained only for a bounded window after completion; apply/frontier/save/mlflow re-touch them via touch_heavy_objects and fail loudly (400) if already evicted — they are never fabricated.

Ratebook /apply is unsupported by contract: RatebookResult has no per-quote dataframe, so /apply is gated at the route (422) AND defended in depth before apply_from_grid, because apply_from_grid would silently ignore solved factor tables.

Apply neutral-miss policy: a ratebook factor level the solver never saw keeps factor 1.0 (onMissing=neutral, no defaultValue) but is LOUD — counted, logged, and flagged 'unseen' in the explainer; it never fails the whole apply.
None constraint thresholds are frontier-only markers: solve()/apply() reject them; frontier() requires a matching threshold_ranges entry per None constraint.
scenario_value std degenerate convention: a single-quote result has std=0.0 (population stat), not null, because the response schema requires a number (_compute_scenario_value_stats).

internal_dataflow: "IN: OptimiserSolveRequest{graph, node_id, source, streaming_chunk_size}. start() flattens the graph, finds the OPTIMISER node, reads node.data.config, validates config -> mode. A solve job is registered (single-flight on (graph_fingerprint,node_id)) BEFORE heavy work so long local runs stay pollable. Background setup thread: execute_lazy_graph runs the pipeline up to the optimiser's data_input (with an opportunistic optimiser_setup dataframe-execution cache request) -> lazy_outputs; _resolve_data_source picks the configured data_input (or sole parent); _validate_and_project does a single streaming pass to reject null quote_id + non-finite objective/constraint/scenario values, then projects+casts solver columns; for ratebook, _extract_factors sinks the banding source's projected factor columns to a parquet artifact (handle). scored_lf is sunk to a temp parquet and build_grid_from_parquet_chunked builds the QuoteGrid (chunk size from a byte-budget policy keyed off execution-profile memory). The grid (and ratebook factor contexts) hand off to a SOLVER background thread. ONLINE: OnlineOptimiser.solve -> solve_online_py / solve_from_grid_py (Lagrangian dual). RATEBOOK: build factor contexts (fingerprint-aligned), RatebookOptimiser.solve -> run_cd_pass_py (full CD pass in Rust). _finalize_solve_result builds the result dict (totals, baseline, lambdas, converged, scenario-value stats+histogram from optimal_scenario_value), OPTIONALLY computes the frontier inline if frontier_enabled, persists the apply-result + ratebook-factor artifacts behind handles, and atomically transitions the job to completed with heavy objects (solver, solve_result, quote_grid) retained for a bounded window. OUT: status endpoint returns the result summary + capped frontier payload + execution_metrics. FRONTIER recompute: re-touch solver+grid, enforce compute budget, solver.frontier(threshold_ranges,...), cap to FRONTIER_POINT_LIMIT, store points, invalidate stale per-point apply artifacts. FRONTIER-SELECT/APPLY: reconstruct a point's result dict from stored points (lambdas parsed from lambda_* fields); ratebook points are re-solved on demand (solver.solve with _constraints_override) and factor tables re-serialised; online apply points run apply_from_grid and persist a per-point artifact. AUTO-RANGE: reads quote_id+constraint columns; per quote independently chooses min/max scenario; reduced in bounded batches to per-quote extrema, hash-partitioned to disk buckets (so quotes split across read batches recombine), then bucket totals summed -> achievable (min,max) envelope per constraint. A streaming variant chunks BEFORE scenario expansion when a chunk-local plan can be proven. APPLY/SAVE/MLFLOW: build optimiser_result.json payload (lambdas, totals, constraints, factor tables for ratebook) and write to a sandbox-validated path or MLflow run."
concurrency_model: "Heavily concurrent and the dominant risk surface. Each solve/auto-range runs across two daemon threads (setup, then solver) plus the request thread. Shared state is a process-global in-memory JobStore (one singleton per 'optimiser' prefix). Writes go through atomic_update / atomic_update_if_heavy_present which build a NEW dict and swap it in under a _write_lock; readers (status polling) rely on CPython GIL atomicity of dict.__setitem__ to see either old or new, never partial. expected_status guards prevent a timeout/supersede from clobbering a completed result. Job admission/cancellation: ExecutionCancellationToken + CancellableJobRegistry (per-job 'latest' registration that supersedes older same-key jobs) for solve, auto-range and graph-node-setup, each polled via _raise_if_*_stopped at checkpoints between phases. A SingleFlightCoordinator on (GRAPH_NODE_SETUP, node_id, graph_fingerprint) serialises setup for the same graph/node; _check_no_concurrent_jobs rejects a second BLOCKING solve (estimate/auto-range are non-blocking). Heavy runtime objects (solver/solve_result/quote_grid/ratebook contexts) have a separate retention timer; after expiry they are stripped, and apply/frontier/save/mlflow re-acquire via touch_heavy_objects (failing 400 if gone). Background threads deliberately use direct store.jobs.get(...) in a few spots (e.g. _finalize_solve_result M6 comment) to avoid triggering eviction from the worker thread. Extensive artifact-orphan cleanup in finally/except blocks handles races where a job's atomic completion update is skipped (superseded) after artifacts were already written."
perf_characteristics: "Designed for large local datasets under bounded memory. Numerical kernels are Rust (solve_online_py / run_cd_pass_py) operating on f32 grids; the ratebook CD pass keeps residuals/multipliers Rust-side to avoid ~max_cd*n_factors*2 PyO3 round-trips of 100k-element buffers per solve. Grid/factor materialisation is parquet-sink + chunked-read with chunk size derived from a byte budget (target chunk bytes scaled from the execution profile's memory limit, clamped 16MiB..512MiB). Validation, estimate and auto-range are single streaming-aggregation passes with projection pushdown (estimate folds the null-quote_id check into the same group_by scan). Auto-range avoids a global per-quote table by hash-partitioning per-batch extrema to disk buckets then reducing per bucket; a streaming variant chunks before scenario expansion to cap peak rows when the suffix is provably chunk-local. Frontier is O(n_points_per_dim ** n_constraints) full solves; capped at 10000 grid points (compute budget) and 2000 returned points (response cap). Frontier warm-starting: ratebook uses nearest-neighbour visit order + linear lambda predictor-corrector; online ratio/unswept sweeps use sequential warm-start. Apply preview capped at 100 rows. Large apply/detail dataframes and ratebook factors are spilled to parquet artifacts behind handles rather than held in the (memory-resident) job dict."

complexity_hotspots.what: End-to-end solve setup orchestration with ~7 distinct terminal-failure exception arms (BackgroundJobStopped, HTTP 4xx/5xx, admission/memory, bounded-memory-unsupported, generic) each mapping to a different lifecycle transition + execution-metrics payload + artifact cleanup; the finally arm releases three registries + single-flight + orphan ratebook artifact.

Two ~250-line near-parallel auto-range drivers (standard vs pre-expansion streaming) with duplicated progress/cancellation/exception/lifecycle scaffolding; the streaming path threads a chunk plan, per-chunk validate+project, and a disk-bucket accumulator.
Hash-partitioned, disk-backed per-quote min/max aggregation with bucket combine/total expr sets; the numerical correctness of the achievable envelope depends on this recombination.

_canonical_ratebook_table_level / _serialise_ratebook_factor_table_rows: combinatorial candidate matching of solver-emitted level reprs against canonical count keys, with minimal-collapse winner selection and loud failure on ambiguity; subtle and correctness-critical for apply alignment.
Shared result finalisation with inline optional frontier compute, dual artifact persistence, atomic completion, and multi-branch orphan cleanup when the completion update is skipped.
Builds the dataframe-execution cache request including the AUTO_RANGE->solver column-superset merge that the cache-key reuse invariant depends on.

On-demand re-solve of a ratebook frontier point and online per-point apply-artifact materialisation, each with cached-result fast paths, heavy-object touch guards, atomic-if-heavy-present updates, and 409 races.

Decorates a Rust SolveResult to recompute actual ratios for ratio constraints, including a pure-Python per-iteration Lagrangian-argmax replay for history (route (b)); the most numerically subtle wrapper, with a special final-iteration alignment rule.
Predictor-corrector frontier sweep: NN ordering, linear lambda extrapolation along prev2->prev, unswept-axis handling, per-point constraint override, points re-sorted to cartesian order.

candidate_risks.concern: Auto-range silently DROPS entire read-batches whose quote_id column contains any null, then reports the dropped count only via a post-hoc null_quote_id_count check at finish().
candidate_risks.why: _ScenarioFrontierRangeAccumulator.add_batch returns early for the whole batch when null_count>0 (lines ~1462-1465), incrementing null_quote_id_count by the null count but excluding ALL rows in that batch (including non-null quotes) from bucket aggregation. finish() raises if null_quote_id_count>0, so behaviour is to fail — but if a future change makes that non-fatal, or if batching interacts with the streaming variant differently, non-null quotes in a tainted batch would be silently excluded from the min/max envelope. The fail-vs-include asymmetry is subtle and the dropped-rows accounting only covers the null rows, not the co-batched valid rows.

candidate_risks.concern: Canonical level resolution picks the candidate that collapses the FEWEST components and FAILS on ties; correctness of apply-time rate lookup hinges on the claim that ties are impossible for single-dtype frames.
candidate_risks.why: _canonical_ratebook_table_level builds float/verbatim candidate combinations per component and asserts the minimal-collapse winner is unique. If a real (e.g. mixed-dtype, or string column whose literal values look like collapsible floats such as '25.0' and '25' both present as counted levels) factor column reaches here, it raises ValueError mid-save and the whole solve result becomes unsaveable, OR—if counts were built from a different frame than the solver grouped on—could mis-map a level to the wrong canonical key and silently apply the wrong rate. The level_counts must describe exactly the solved frame; any divergence is a silent-correctness hazard.

candidate_risks.concern: Legacy frontier_min/frontier_max changed meaning: comment says they are 'no longer treated as a multiplier on baseline values' and are now absolute, applied to every constraint.
candidate_risks.why: _auto_frontier_ranges_from_config returns {cname:(frontier_min,frontier_max) for cname in constraints} — the SAME absolute range for every constraint. For multi-constraint configs with different scales (e.g. premium total vs loss-ratio), a single shared absolute (min,max) is almost certainly wrong for at least one axis, and the silent fallback (when frontier_ranges is absent but frontier_min/max present) could produce a misleading frontier rather than erroring. Worth auditing whether any saved configs still carry the legacy pair and what the frontend emits.

candidate_risks.concern: Opportunistic AUTO_RANGE cache warming advertises solver-required columns in the cache key while executing with the narrower auto-range projection demand; relies on the auto_range ⊆ solver subset invariant AND on a runtime seed-time column check to reject mismatches.
candidate_risks.why: If the subset invariant is ever violated (e.g. a future constraint/objective column added to auto-range but not solver projection, or a node that drops columns between the two profiles), a later solve could HIT a cache artifact that lacks solver columns, or reuse an artifact whose contents differ from what the solver needs. The code itself flags this as load-bearing (comment lines ~4199-4240). A subtle projection regression here would surface as wrong solver input or an opaque rebuild, not a clear error.

candidate_risks.concern: Background worker reads/writes job dict via a mix of atomic_update(expected_status=...) and direct store.jobs.get(...) (M6), and several apply/frontier paths do touch_heavy_objects -> require_completed_job -> read solver/grid as separate steps.
candidate_risks.why: Between touch_heavy_objects (which extends the retention window) and the subsequent require_completed_job + .get('solver'), the heavy-object timer or a concurrent clear_result_data/atomic completion could still race; the code mitigates with atomic_update_if_heavy_present and 409s, but the multi-step get patterns in _ratebook_runtime_state_or_raise and _materialise_frontier_point_apply are intricate and a missed re-check could surface a None solver as a 500 or, worse, operate on partially-cleared state. High-value area for a focused concurrency audit.

candidate_risks.concern: Frontier point lambdas are reconstructed by string-prefix parsing of lambda_* fields and constraint values from total_*/constraints/bare-name keys, with finite-float coercion; ratebook points are then RE-SOLVED rather than using stored optima.
candidate_risks.why: _frontier_point_lambdas/_frontier_point_constraint_value/_frontier_point_constraints_override pull values from heterogeneous dict shapes. A frontier point whose stored schema differs slightly (e.g. a constraint named 'total_x' colliding with the total_ prefix convention, or a lambda key collision) could parse the wrong value. For ratebook, _materialise_ratebook_frontier_point re-runs solver.solve with _constraints_override derived from threshold_* fields — so the displayed/saved factor tables depend on re-solving converging to the same point the frontier sweep found; warm-start differences could yield a slightly different optimum than the frontier row implies.

candidate_risks.concern: Ratio-constraint history is reconstructed by replaying the Lagrangian argmax in pure Python on the linearised DataFrame for each iteration's recorded lambdas, asserted to reproduce the Rust solver's per-iteration optimal_steps.
candidate_risks.why: The replay assumes the recorded lambdas are the pre-update lambdas used for that iteration's argmax and that the argmax is deterministic given lambdas+grid, with a special-cased final-iteration substitution for the non-converged averaged-lambda pass. Any drift between the Python replay's sign convention/precision (f32 vs f64) and the Rust argmax would silently mis-report history ratios. record_history is opt-in/off by default, limiting blast radius, but it is a genuine reimplementation-equivalence hazard.

candidate_risks.concern: _optimiser_service.py is ~5046 LOC and optimiser.py ~1803 LOC; a single module mixes pure helpers, artifact path/security validation, concurrency primitives, numerical-canonicalisation logic, and 4 large exception-handling orchestrators with heavily duplicated failure-mapping scaffolding.
candidate_risks.why: The two auto-range drivers, the solve setup driver, and the solver background all repeat ~10-arm exception->lifecycle-transition+metrics+cleanup blocks. Duplication of the terminal-reason mapping and orphan-cleanup logic is a maintenance and correctness hazard: a fix to one failure arm can easily be missed in the parallel copies, and the sheer size obscures the invariants. This is the explicit 'god-file architecture question' — strong candidate for extraction (artifact lifecycle, auto-range engine, ratebook factor-table serialisation, failure-mapping) into cohesive modules.

candidate_risks.concern: When frontier_enabled, the inline frontier compute in _finalize_solve_result catches ALL exceptions and records them only as a non-fatal result['frontier_error'] string while the solve still completes successfully.
candidate_risks.why: A genuine numerical/feasibility problem in the frontier (e.g. infeasible ranges, solver divergence, a real bug) is downgraded to a warning string the user may not notice, and the primary solve is reported as fully successful. This is broad-except error-swallowing on a numerical path; the project's stated philosophy prefers loud failure. Worth auditing whether frontier failures should at least surface as a distinct job warning state vs being buried in the result dict.

candidate_risks.concern: Server-owned artifact handles are validated against a temp-root and structural rules, but the validation relies on Path.resolve(strict=exists) and is_relative_to checks; handles are read back from the (in-memory) job dict and re-validated on every load/cleanup.
candidate_risks.why: The validation looks robust (absolute-path requirement, null-byte rejection, parent==root, prefix+filename checks). The residual lead is whether any path component could be a symlink created between persist and load that resolves outside root, or whether resolve(strict=False) on a non-existent path (used when the dir was already cleaned) could bypass the is_relative_to check. Lower priority given handles are server-generated (mkdtemp under a fixed root), not user-supplied, but the load/cleanup-from-job-dict pattern means a corrupted job dict is the trust boundary.

candidate_risks.concern: Estimate path deliberately does NOT run solve-grade NaN/inf value validation (only column presence, quote_id dtype, and null-quote_id), so estimate can report counts for data the subsequent solve will reject.
candidate_risks.why: Intentional cost trade-off (single scan) and documented, but it means the estimate and solve disagree on validity: a user sees a clean estimate then the solve fails on non-finite values. Not a correctness bug per se, but a UX/contract-divergence lead — and if any caller treats a successful estimate as a solvability guarantee, that assumption is unsound.

test_coverage_observations: "Substantial dedicated test surface: tests/test_optimiser_routes.py, test_optimiser_routes_critical_edges.py, test_optimiser_routes_real_library.py (pins route<->library contracts incl. frontier compute cap == max_total_points), test_optimiser_service_validation.py, test_optimiser_frontier_materialisation.py, test_optimiser_ratebook_apply_agreement.py (apply<->save agreement), test_optimiser_apply.py / _apply_artifacts.py / _apply_trace_enrichment.py, test_optimiser_contracts.py, test_optimiser_golden.py + golden fixtures (online/ratebook artifacts), test_optimiser_io.py, performance/test_optimiser_memory_response_perf.py. UI-contract JSON fixtures exist for every response shape. Frontend has optimiserHelpers/ratebookFactorTables/scenarioStats unit tests and panel store-integration tests. Repro scripts (repro/benchmark_optimiser_*, price_contour_ratebook_frontier, output/price_contour_frontier_repro) suggest prior frontier-duplicate and ratebook-frontier bugs were investigated. Gaps worth probing in a deep audit: (1) concurrency/race tests around heavy-object eviction interleaved with apply/frontier/save (the multi-step touch->get patterns); (2) auto-range null-quote co-batch exclusion behaviour and the streaming-vs-standard auto-range equivalence on the same input; (3) ratebook canonical-level tie/ambiguity and mixed-dtype factor columns end-to-end through save->apply; (4) inline-frontier failure surfacing (frontier_error swallowing). The bundled price_contour numerical kernels are Rust and not unit-tested from this repo (only via integration through the routes)."
